properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 13 at 1:57AM EDT until September 13 at 6:00PM EDT by NWS Boston/Norton MA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Rhode Island and southeast Massachusetts.

* WHEN...From 5 AM EDT early this morning through this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of low-lying and
flood-prone locations. Flooding may occur in poor drainage and
urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Showers and a few embedded thunderstorms with localized narrow
bands of torrential rainfall overspread the region this morning.
Widespread rainfall amounts of 0.50 to 2 inches are expected.
However...localized narrow bands of 2-4" of rain are possible
within a 3 hour period. While it remains uncertain if these
narrow bands of heavier rain occur...the potential exists for
localized flash flooding...especially if it were to occur over a
vulnerable urban center.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.areaDesc: Chelan, WA; Douglas, WA; Ferry, WA; Okanogan, WA
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 12 at 7:41PM PDT until September 13 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS Spokane WA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Debris and ash flows, rock slides, and minor flooding caused
by excessive rainfall is possible, especially near burn scars.

* WHERE...Portions of North Central and Northeast Washington,
including the following counties, in North Central Washington,
Chelan, Douglas and Okanogan. In Northeast Washington, Ferry.

* WHEN...From 1 AM PDT Sunday through Sunday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in debris and ash flows over
burn scars in steep terrain.  Rock slides will be possible.  Minor
flooding in urban areas where there is poor drainage. Storm drains
and ditches may become clogged with debris.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A slow moving storm system will bring persistent bands of rain
through Central Washington.  Moderate to heavy rain intensities
are expected at times.  Rainfall amounts will range between 0.50
and 1.50 inches with locally around 2.00 inches in southern
Chelan County.
- This includes but is not limited to the following burn scars:
Modrite, Kaiser Canyon, Sinlahekin, Chelan Falls, Little Giant,
Sisi, and Pioneer.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.
